main_body: Hipped green tile roof (rows ~4-42) over a cream plaster wall with a red beam, red posts and a dark lattice double door (rows ~43-73), on a grey stone base
top_band: Green tile roof slope from the ridge cap at rows 4-9 down to the eave at rows 41-43. It is a large, tiled sloped surface that reads as the top of the building. Tones run from light #8ab8a2 down to dark #1b3836.
evidence: The roof is drawn as a trapezoid with a ridge cap and rows of tiles, so it shows its top slope as a surface, the same way the reference roofs do. Below it come a light eave edge (rows 42-43), a red beam (44-45) with a dark shadow row (46), then the vertical wall and door. The door lattice is darker and sits between projecting posts, so it reads as set back. The roof surface and the front face are both clearly drawn, so the building passes the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 green steps with per-tile highlights, which is good. The weak points are elsewhere. 83% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline has the near-black sticker look rather than a tint of the adjacent material. The cream wall panels and the red posts are large, almost flat areas with only sparse speckle. Overall the piece has 32 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references, and its flat-fill coverage is 5% against 0%. Median colours per tile equal the stone reference (11) but fall below the other reference (18). That adds up to flatter and thinner than the Beodeul standard.
